notice: A ninth held-out set of real documents (the tenth set in all), none in the nine earlier samples (sample.json, sample-heldout.json through sample-heldout8.json), from hosts those samples did not use (no URL, host or SHA-256 of their 498 documents recurs). 50 documents from 48 hosts: 8 letters, 1 e-mail, 6 notices, 5 contracts, 3 orders (two consent orders and a records-council decision), 5 sets of minutes, 4 memoranda, 5 invoices, 2 purchase orders, 5 forms, 4 statements, 2 reports. Gold expects 28 ready, 18 either and 4 needs_review, so readiness is judged on 32. No synthetic document is in the set. Concentration: no host gives more than 2 documents (www.nj.gov: real10-order-02 and -03, from two different bodies; oronocotownship-mn.gov: real10-invoice-01 and -02, from two different vendors); 6 documents are from outside the United States (New Zealand, Ireland, Northern Ireland, England, Ontario). Hosts that are close kin of earlier ones are these: www.dgs.ca.gov, www.auburn.ca.gov and www.eldoradocounty.ca.gov (real10-notice-03, real10-memo-02, real10-notice-05) are under ca.gov, which earlier samples drew on through four other bodies' sites; web.sos.ky.gov (real10-form-02) is under ky.gov, as are psc.ky.gov and transportation.ky.gov; www.whitestown.in.gov and laporteco.in.gov (real10-invoice-03, real10-form-05) are under in.gov, which an earlier sample used directly; the three gov.uk parish and borough sites and gw.govt.nz share only the national suffix with earlier hosts. Party strings an earlier sample also carries are these: 'Office of the Attorney General' and 'OAG' (accepted for New York's office on real10-letter-01) name other offices in real6-letter-06, real8-letter-13, real9-letter-07 and real4-office-08; 'Department of General Services', 'DGS', 'California Department of General Services' and 'State of California' (accepted on real10-notice-03) are carried by real4-office-10 and -11 (the same California department, from a 2016 FOIA release on law.resource.org) and by real4-notice-01 and real7-form-02. How gold was made: one reader wrote gold for each document from its own text (page renders read for scanned or image-only parts: real10-contract-02, real10-contract-05, real10-order-02, real10-minutes-04, real10-letter-08, real10-form-02, real10-form-03, real10-form-05, real10-statement-01 and the logos of real10-invoice-01, real10-memo-04 and real10-statement-02), without any model's reading of it; three second readers each read a third of the set blind, given only the documents and a brief, and wrote gold independently; the two readings were adjudicated against the documents. One primary label was wrong and changed: real10-contract-05, where the first reader took 29 August 2025 for the recording stamp only and the second showed the signature page 'EXECUTED on this the 29 day of August, 2025' (gold now 2025-08-29, with 27 August and 1 August accepted). Otherwise the second readers agreed with the first on type, date and party for all 50 in the sense that each reading accepts the other's answer, after accepted name variants were added (office names such as 'City of San Antonio Office of the City Auditor', board names on minutes, 'for' on filings); they differed on readiness for 9 more documents (kept as the first reader set them, reasons logged), on the sender of real10-notice-01 (the district that issued the notice versus the landfill it was issued to; both accepted, the issuer primary), and on purchase orders (named 'to' the vendor, as earlier samples do; 'from' the buyer accepted); their extra forbidden dates and names were merged, except where a name is an accepted party. The second readers are AI readers of the same family as the first, not people, so the second reading is weaker evidence of independence than a human one, and the adjudicator saw the second readers' lists of documents they marked unsure before adjudicating. Known hard cases: an Irish day-month date (real10-letter-08, 09/06/2025 is 9 June); an undated ministerial letter (real10-letter-04, gold date null); a handwritten notice of violation with violation and service dates (real10-notice-01); publication versus hearing dates (real10-notice-05, -06); cover memos bundled before contracts and awards (real10-contract-02, real10-letter-06); a lease with a recording stamp and hand-amended dates (real10-contract-05); an undated board order (real10-order-02); an e-mail printed from a mailbox whose owner is not the sender (real10-email-01); filled form values that are form fields absent from the text layer (real10-form-02, where a text-only reader cannot see the corporation's name); issuers named only in a logo image (real10-invoice-01, real10-memo-04, real10-statement-02); a bank reconciliation that names no body at all (real10-statement-03, parties empty); and a state pay estimate rather than a vendor invoice (real10-invoice-05). Fetching: every URL was fetched with fetch.py's own user agent and matched its pinned size and SHA-256 on 2026-11-24, but dpw.lacounty.gov (real10-notice-01) answers HTTP 403 to about half of requests, whatever the user agent, so fetch.py may need running again or that file saving by hand; a run without it scores 49. source.page is null throughout: the documents were found by web search, not from a listing page. Hosts that refused or failed while the set was gathered, and so gave nothing: bbhe.az.gov, ourair.org, fremont.gov, vancouver.ca and permits.puyallupwa.gov (403), cityofhomer-ak.gov (connection reset), the City of Berkeley site (502), and several 404s. Licences are per document under source.license; all are public-sector or public-university publications with no licence stated on the file. Only URLs, pins, notes and gold are committed; no document text is. The set was sealed for one candidate, the whole-value confidence score being built on a separate draft branch; no model has read it, and no rule, threshold or prompt has been written from it.
